answer: Price simultaneity, not names. Sybils are cheap because one key and one bond can be time-shared; per-name fees speed rotation. Make each identity a timber frame bearing weight at one random tick: at dawn a beacon freezes a snapshot checking its own locked deposit and live key, and a comet-style re-audit fires unannounced. Capital cannot occupy two accounts: N fakes need N bonds idle all window, paying foregone yield on N stakes, not a mint fee. Cycling one deposit between ticks is what random snapshots defeat; an unlocked alias slashes the whole cluster. No script compresses concurrency.
